newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM sees improved full-yr operating profit.
newsitem.headline: KLM sees improved full-yr operating profit.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Tuesday it expected operating profits for the 1997/98 financial year, ending March 30, to improve.

"As far as operating income for the full fiscal year is concerned, we expect to approximate the level attained in the better years in KLM's recent history," the Dutch flag carrier said in a statement.

KLM said the forecast for the rest of the current financial year was based on the assumption that the present favourable economic conditions would continue and that there would be no substantial change in present exchange rates.
The prognosis also implied the assumption that fuel prices would remain at present levels and that the company's Focus 2000 cost cutting and revenue boosting programme remained on track.
In the first quarter of the 1997/98 financial year, ended June 30, operating income soared to 244 million guilders from 80 million in the year-ago period.
The positive effect of exchange rate changes on the first-quarter operating income totalled 17 million guilders, the company said.
In 1996/97 KLM posted a full-year operating loss after provisions of 201 million guilders, compared with an operating profit of 453 million in the previous year.
The 1996/97 full-year operating income before provision totalled 89 million guilders.
